results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA §13.2. It notes that Norvane may assign to any third party, including a competitor, without notice, while Calder Ridge's own assignment needs consent. The proposed fix makes assignment mutual, requires consent and bars assignment to a Customer competitor. The supply-continuity and confidentiality risk is only implied, not stated, so this is a marginal pass.

The memo cites SA §13.3, the consent requirement and the termination and damages consequences, and it recommends deleting the clause or limiting it to competitor acquirers. However, it does not recognize the pending sale of Calder Ridge. It asks only whether a sale 'is foreseeable', so it neither ties the risk to the planned sale nor recommends getting consent or a waiver before signing or closing.
Identifies the OF §2.2 three-year evergreen renewal with a 30-day notice window, explains the lock-in, and proposes a one-year renewal with a 90-day opt-out and a reminder obligation.
Identifies that SA §9.3 carves Customer's indemnity out of the cap, leaving it uncapped while Norvane stays capped. Recommends rewriting §9.3 to apply mutually and narrowing §10.1.
Correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§9.1), Delaware law, and a three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.
States that SA §1.3 ranks the SA first, then the OF, then the Spec, and applies this to the renewal conflict and the invoice-timing conflict.
Issues are tiered (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW). Change of control and uncapped indemnity are marked CRITICAL, and the memo suggests raising Issues 1–3 first.
Each issue sets out the location, the problem and why it matters, and a fix with proposed language. A separate section at the end lists business decisions and clarifications needed from Calder Ridge.

Flags the Specifications Schedule heavily: Issue 1 rates the mismatch CRITICAL and calls Spec §1 circular, and Issue 11 raises QA gaps in the Spec. It also cites outside authority (6 Del. C. § 2-316).
